The provider reads those files, converts them to our shared session format, and renders markdown.\n\nThe provider covers the same commands as the claude and codex providers.\n\n- `check`, `sync`, `list`, `watch`, `run`, and `reindex` all work.\n- Reconstruction works in both directions. We can rebuild another agent's session as a qwen session, and `qwen --resume` accepts the file we write. We can also turn a qwen session into another agent's native format.\n- The common tools get dedicated markdown formatting. Shell commands show their raw output. Edits show a diff. Todo lists show a checklist. Subagent calls show the prompt and the result.\n\n## How we tested it\n\nEvery command above was run against real sessions from the installed qwen binary, not only unit tests. We ran qwen through error cases, permission denials, parallel tool calls, subagent spawns, manual context compaction, and slash commands. We also installed qwen-code 0.21.0 and 0.20.1 from npm and confirmed they write the same file format. They are normal tool calls inside the parent transcript.\n- Context compaction appends one system record and never rewrites the file, so the append-only parser is safe.\n- Slash commands are never recorded as user turns, so no trimming is needed.\n\n## What is not fully tested\n\nThese are the open gaps for resume and cloud. 1\nspecstory-cli/pkg/providers/qwencode/provider.go:165-167\n**Session lookup escapes project scope**\n\nA `--session` value containing traversal segments such as `../../../../external-transcript` is joined directly into the selected project's chat path. `filepath.Join` cleans those segments, and the subsequent `Stat` and `ParseSessionFile` calls read the resulting file even when it is outside that project's `chats` directory. This allows a readable transcript from another local project to be retrieved and synced. # Qwen Code Authentication Options

````text
## 1. Qwen OAuth (Discontinued)
**Status**: Free tier ended April 15, 2026. No longer available in the `/auth` dialog.

Previously required a `qwen.ai` account with browser-based login. Users should migrate to alternative options.

## 2. Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan
**Setup**: Interactive via `/auth` or environment variables

**Environment variables**:
```bash
export BAILIAN_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY="sk-sp-xxxxxxxxx"
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://coding.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1"
export OPENAI_MODEL="qwen3-coder-plus"
```

**settings.json snippet**:
```json
{
  "modelProviders": {
    "openai": [{
      "id": "qwen3-coder-plus",
      "baseUrl": "https://coding.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1",
      "envKey": "BAILIAN_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY"
    }]
  }
}
```

**Models included**: qwen3.5-plus, qwen3.6-plus, qwen3.7-plus, qwen3-coder variants, glm-5, kimi-k2.5, MiniMax-M2.5

**Regions**: Beijing and International endpoints available

## 3. Alibaba Cloud Token Plan
**Setup**: Via `/auth` or environment variables

**Environment variables**:
```bash
export BAILIAN_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY="your-api-key"
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1"
export OPENAI_MODEL="qwen3.7-plus"
```

**Billing**: Usage-based (tokens consumed)

**Regional endpoints**:
- China: `https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`
- International: `https://token-plan.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`

## 4. API Key (Flexible)
Supports multiple protocols via `modelProviders` in settings.json.

**Supported protocols**:

| Protocol | Key | Default Env Var | Providers |
|----------|-----|-----------------|-----------|
| OpenAI-compatible | `openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI, Azure, OpenRouter, Requesty, ModelScope |
| Anthropic | `anthropic` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Claude models |
| Google GenAI | `gemini` | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Gemini |
| Vertex AI | `vertex-ai` | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or ADC | Google Vertex AI |

**Complete settings.json example**:
```json
{
  "modelProviders": {
    "openai": [{
      "id": "gpt-4o",
      "baseUrl": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
      "envKey": "OPENAI_API_KEY"
    }],
    "anthropic": [{
      "id": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
      "envKey": "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
    }]
  },
  "security": {
    "auth": {
      "selectedType": "openai"
    }
  },
  "model": {
    "name": "gpt-4o"
  }
}
```

**Environment variable priority** (highest to lowest):
1. Shell `export` / CLI flags
2. `.qwen/.env` or `.env` files
3. `settings.json` → `env` field

## Third-Party Providers via `/auth`
Pre-configured options include DeepSeek, Grok, MiniMax, Z.AI, Kimi, Idealab, ModelScope, OpenRouter, and Requesty.

## Local Ollama
Documentation doesn't explicitly cover Ollama configuration in this authentication guide; consult the Custom Provider section for self-hosted endpoints.
````

_**Agent (claude-fable-5-1 2026-09-14 21:59:36Z)**_

Here's what you need.

**Install via Homebrew**

Homebrew core has the formula, currently at 0.23.3, bottled, with node and ripgrep as dependencies. You already have Node 22 via nvm, but the brew formula brings its own.

```zsh
brew install qwen-code
qwen --version
```

One thing to note for the PR review: Greg tested the file format against qwen-code 0.20.1 and 0.21.0. Homebrew will give you 0.23.3, so it's worth confirming the JSONL under `~/.qwen/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/chats/` still matches what the parser expects.

**Accounts and payment**

The free Qwen OAuth login is gone. The docs say the free tier ended April 15, 2026 and it no longer appears in the `/auth` dialog. So you need an API key from somewhere. Your options, roughly in order of least friction for you:

- **Use a key you already have.** Qwen Code speaks the Anthropic protocol natively, so an existing Anthropic API key works with no new account. Same for an OpenAI or Gemini key, or OpenRouter. For testing the SpecStory provider this is my recommendation, because what we care about is Qwen Code's session file format, not which model answers.
- **Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan.** A flat-rate subscription with Qwen3-coder and Qwen3.x-plus models, plus GLM, Kimi, and MiniMax. Requires an Alibaba Cloud Model Studio account with international billing set up. Pick this if you want the sessions to reflect real Qwen models, since tool call shapes could differ slightly by model.
- **Alibaba Cloud Token Plan.** Same account, usage-based billing instead of a subscription.

**Configuring auth with an Anthropic key**

Run `qwen` in a project directory, type `/auth`, and choose the Anthropic protocol option. Or set it via environment and settings:

```zsh
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."
```

```json
{
  "modelProviders": {
    "anthropic": [{ "id": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514", "envKey": "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" }]
  },
  "security": { "auth": { "selectedType": "anthropic" } },
  "model": { "name": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514" }
}
```

That goes in `~/.qwen/settings.json`. Model IDs in the docs example are stale, so substitute a current one. Qwen Code also reads a `.qwen/.env` file in the project, which is handy if you'd rather not export the key globally.

**Recommendation**

Install with brew, point it at your Anthropic key via `/auth`, and run a short session with a shell command, a file edit, and a todo list so the PR's markdown formatting paths all get exercised. If you later want to verify the Qwen-model-specific path, the Coding Plan is the cheap add-on.

```text
# Qwen Code Authentication Options

## The Three Main Paths in `/auth`

### 1. Alibaba ModelStudio
This opens a sub-menu with three tiers:
- **Coding Plan** (individual developers with weekly quota)
- **Token Plan** (teams/companies with usage-based billing)
- **Standard API Key** (existing ModelStudio keys)

### 2. Third-party Providers
Built-in options include: "DeepSeek, Grok, MiniMax, Z.AI, Kimi, Idealab, ModelScope, OpenRouter, Requesty." Note that Anthropic/Claude is **not** listed here as a pre-built option.

### 3. Custom Provider
Requires manual setup for unsupported services. Based on the documentation, you manually specify:
- Protocol type (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or other compatible formats)
- Base URL
- API key
- Model identifier

## Using Anthropic Claude Directly

To use an Anthropic API key with Qwen Code, choose **Custom Provider** rather than a pre-built third-party entry. Then configure it via `~/.qwen/settings.json` by setting the protocol to `"anthropic"`, specifying your key in `envKey: "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"`, and providing the model ID (e.g., `"claude-sonnet-4-20250514"`).
```

_**Agent (claude-fable-5-1 2026-09-14 22:10:23Z)**_

Pick **Custom Provider**. That's where the Anthropic protocol lives. Anthropic isn't a built-in under Third-party Providers, which only lists DeepSeek, Grok, MiniMax, Z.AI, Kimi, Idealab, ModelScope, OpenRouter, and Requesty.

In the Custom Provider flow it will ask for:

1. **Protocol** – choose Anthropic.
2. **Base URL** – leave the default, or `https://api.anthropic.com` if it insists on one.
3. **API key** – paste your Anthropic key.
4. **Model ID** – a current Claude model id. `claude-sonnet-5` is a good balance of cost and tool-use quality for generating test sessions.

If the interactive flow fights you, quit and write this to `~/.qwen/settings.json` instead, then export the key in your shell:

```json
{
  "modelProviders": {
    "anthropic": [{ "id": "claude-sonnet-5", "envKey": "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" }]
  },
  "security": { "auth": { "selectedType": "anthropic" } },
  "model": { "name": "claude-sonnet-5" }
}
```

```zsh
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."
qwen
```

Two other things in your screenshot worth noting:

- **Auto mode is on** by default, with an LLM classifier deciding which tool calls to approve. That's fine for a scratch project, but run it somewhere disposable rather than in the specstory-cli checkout while you're generating test sessions.
- The **Alibaba ModelStudio** path is the one to come back to if you decide you want real Qwen models in the recorded sessions. It needs an Alibaba Cloud account with billing.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5-1 2026-09-14 22:11:24Z)**_

Yes, accept it. That's the default Qwen Code ships for the Anthropic protocol, so its client is built to append the `messages` endpoint to that base correctly.

The only way it would be wrong is if the first request comes back as a 404 on a path like `/v1/v1/messages`. If that happens, edit the base URL to `https://api.anthropic.com` with no `/v1` suffix, either back in `/auth` or in `~/.qwen/settings.json`. Otherwise you're good to send a first prompt.

<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Disable Anthropic prompt-cache tagging in Qwen settings

```bash
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'EOF'
import json,os
p=os.path.expanduser('~/.qwen/settings.json')
d=json.load(open(p))
d.setdefault('model',{}).setdefault('generationConfig',{})['enableCacheControl']=False
for e in d['modelProviders']['anthropic']:
    e.setdefault('generationConfig',{})['enableCacheControl']=False
json.dump(d,open(p,'w'),indent=2)
print(json.dumps(d['model'],indent=2))
print([e['generationConfig']['enableCacheControl'] for e in d['modelProviders']['anthropic']])
EOF
```

_**Agent (claude-fable-5-1 2026-09-14 22:17:16Z)**_

Done. Prompt caching is now disabled for the Anthropic provider in `~/.qwen/settings.json`. Restart Qwen Code and re-send the prompt. Ctrl+Y alone probably won't pick up the settings change, so a fresh launch is safer.

**What was wrong.** Qwen Code 0.23.3 has a bug in its Anthropic client. When it detects a native Anthropic base URL, it marks the system prompt with a global cache scope but only marks the last tool definition that way. The Anthropic API requires every block before a globally scoped one to be globally scoped too, and tools come before the system prompt on the wire, so the request is rejected. This only bites when talking to Anthropic directly, which is why Greg didn't see it testing with other backends.

**What I changed.** I set the `enableCacheControl` flag to false at the top-level model config and on each of the three provider entries. That drops all cache tagging, so there's no scope to get wrong. The cost is no prompt-cache discount, which is fine for generating test sessions.

**Fallback if it still fails.** Adding `/v1` back to the base URL will not work, but pointing at Anthropic through OpenRouter under Third-party Providers would sidestep this code path entirely, since the global scope is only attached for a native Anthropic hostname.
